title: The Majesty of Solomon
description: The Majesty of Solomon in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 113, headed “The same”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The maj-es-ty of So-lo-mon! How glo-rious to be-hold The ser-vants wait-ing round his throne, Th'i-vo-ry and the gold.

lines: The servants waiting round his throne,
But, mighty God, thy palace shines
Thine angel-guards are swift as winds,
Soon as thine only Son had made
And when oppress'd with pains and fears
On the cold ground he lies,
Now to the hands of Christ our King
They wait upon his saints, and bring
Pleasure and praise run thro' their host
Then Satan has a captive lost,
But there's an hour of brighter joy,
O! could I say, without a doubt,
There shall my soul be found,
Then let the great archangel shout,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
